thread.title: Facebook, Google, Apple dip in another rollercoaster day on Wall Street

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Facebook, Google, Apple dip in another rollercoaster day on Wall Street

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high technology index

text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 7, 2018, 2:01pm PST Shares in Silicon Valley's biggest public companies took another downward turn on Wednesday as the U.S. stock market continued its rollercoaster ride. The S&P 500 closed the day down 0.5 percent after surging as much as 1.2 percent earlier — marking its biggest single-day reversal in two years. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged as much as 381 points and plummeted as much as 127 points during the day, before closing down 19.42 points. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology Index dipped 1.69 percent on Wednesday, led by declines at Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT), down 3.1 percent; Facebook (NASDAQ: FB), which fell 2.77 percent; Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG), down 2.68 percent; and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), which dropped 2.18 percent. Only two companies on the Bloomberg index of Silicon Valley's 13 largest technology stocks closed up, and then just barely: Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC), up 0.65 percent, and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), up 0.42 percent. Among all Silicon Valley-based stocks, the worst performers on Wednesday were: • Netgear (NASDAQ: NTGR) plunged 15.36 percent. The San Jose-based networking equipment maker posted a fourth-quarter loss yesterday and said it would do an IPO for its Arlo security camera business later this year — news that initially drove shares 5 percent higher in after-hours trading on Tuesday. • Maxim Integrated Products (NASDAQ: MXIM) slumped 4.5 percent. The stock surged last week after a CNBC report said that Japanese chipmaker Renesas Electronics Corp. was kicking the tires on a potential purchase. Maxim's stock quickly deflated , however, after Renesas issued a statement denying acquisition talks. • Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ: LRCX) fell 3.76 percent. The best performers among all Silicon Valley stocks: • Roku (NASDAQ: ROKU) rose 9.05 percent. The Los Gatos company has been one of the region's most volatile stocks this year after its September 2017 IPO. The stock is still up more than 150 percent since its Wall Street debut. • Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE) shares continued their surge from the previous day . The Milpitas-based manufacturer is riding high on reports that its record second-quarter revenue, up 52 percent, was helped by a $200 million order of 3-D sensing lasers that analysts speculate went to iPhone maker Apple. • Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET) gained 3.39 percent. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 7, 2018, 2:01pm PST Related Content
